34:class KeyboardButton(TelegramObject):
35:    """
36:    This object represents one button of the reply keyboard. At most one of the optional fields
37:    must be used to specify type of the button. For simple text buttons, :obj:`str`
38:    can be used instead of this object to specify text of the button.
39:
40:    Objects of this class are comparable in terms of equality. Two objects of this class are
41:    considered equal, if their :attr:`text`, :attr:`request_contact`, :attr:`request_location`,
42:    :attr:`request_poll`, :attr:`web_app`, :attr:`request_users` and :attr:`request_chat` are
43:    equal.
44:
45:    Note:
46:        * Optional fields are mutually exclusive.
47:        * :attr:`request_contact` and :attr:`request_location` options will only work in Telegram
48:          versions released after 9 April, 2016. Older clients will display unsupported message.
49:        * :attr:`request_poll` option will only work in Telegram versions released after 23
50:          January, 2020. Older clients will display unsupported message.
51:        * :attr:`web_app` option will only work in Telegram versions released after 16 April, 2022.
52:          Older clients will display unsupported message.
53:        * :attr:`request_users` and :attr:`request_chat` options will only work in Telegram
54:          versions released after 3 February, 2023. Older clients will display unsupported
55:          message.
56:
57:    .. versionchanged:: 21.0
58:       Removed deprecated argument and attribute ``request_user``.
59:    .. versionchanged:: 20.0
60:       :attr:`web_app` is considered as well when comparing objects of this type in terms of
61:       equality.
62:    .. versionchanged:: 20.5
63:       :attr:`request_users` and :attr:`request_chat` are considered as well when
64:       comparing objects of this type in terms of equality.
65:
66:    Args:
67:        text (:obj:`str`): Text of the button. If none of the optional fields are used, it will be
68:            sent to the bot as a message when the button is pressed.
69:        request_contact (:obj:`bool`, optional): If :obj:`True`, the user's phone number will be
70:            sent as a contact when the button is pressed. Available in private chats only.
71:        request_location (:obj:`bool`, optional): If :obj:`True`, the user's current location will
72:            be sent when the button is pressed. Available in private chats only.
73:        request_poll (:class:`~telegram.KeyboardButtonPollType`, optional): If specified, the user
74:            will be asked to create a poll and send it to the bot when the button is pressed.
75:            Available in private chats only.
76:        web_app (:class:`~telegram.WebAppInfo`, optional): If specified, the described `Web App
77:            <https://core.telegram.org/bots/webapps>`_ will be launched when the button is pressed.
78:            The Web App will be able to send a :attr:`Message.web_app_data` service message.
79:            Available in private chats only.
80:
81:            .. versionadded:: 20.0
82:
83:        request_users (:class:`KeyboardButtonRequestUsers`, optional): If specified, pressing the
84:            button will open a list of suitable users. Tapping on any user will send its
85:            identifier to the bot in a :attr:`telegram.Message.users_shared` service message.
86:            Available in private chats only.
87:
88:            .. versionadded:: 20.8
89:        request_chat (:class:`KeyboardButtonRequestChat`, optional): If specified, pressing the
90:            button will open a list of suitable chats. Tapping on a chat will send its
91:            identifier to the bot in a :attr:`telegram.Message.chat_shared` service message.
92:            Available in private chats only.
93:
94:            .. versionadded:: 20.1
95:    Attributes:
96:        text (:obj:`str`): Text of the button. If none of the optional fields are used, it will be
97:            sent to the bot as a message when the button is pressed.
98:        request_contact (:obj:`bool`): Optional. If :obj:`True`, the user's phone number will be
99:            sent as a contact when the button is pressed. Available in private chats only.
100:        request_location (:obj:`bool`): Optional. If :obj:`True`, the user's current location will
101:            be sent when the button is pressed. Available in private chats only.
102:        request_poll (:class:`~telegram.KeyboardButtonPollType`): Optional. If specified,
103:            the user will be asked to create a poll and send it to the bot when the button is
104:            pressed. Available in private chats only.
105:        web_app (:class:`~telegram.WebAppInfo`): Optional. If specified, the described `Web App
106:            <https://core.telegram.org/bots/webapps>`_ will be launched when the button is pressed.
107:            The Web App will be able to send a :attr:`Message.web_app_data` service message.
108:            Available in private chats only.
109:
110:            .. versionadded:: 20.0
111:        request_users (:class:`KeyboardButtonRequestUsers`): Optional. If specified, pressing the
112:            button will open a list of suitable users. Tapping on any user will send its
113:            identifier to the bot in a :attr:`telegram.Message.users_shared` service message.
114:            Available in private chats only.
115:
116:            .. versionadded:: 20.8
117:        request_chat (:class:`KeyboardButtonRequestChat`): Optional. If specified, pressing the
118:            button will open a list of suitable chats. Tapping on a chat will send its
119:            identifier to the bot in a :attr:`telegram.Message.chat_shared` service message.
120:            Available in private chats only.
121:
122:            .. versionadded:: 20.1
123:    """
124:
125:    __slots__ = (
126:        "request_chat",
127:        "request_contact",
128:        "request_location",
129:        "request_poll",
130:        "request_users",

136:        self,
137:        text: str,
138:        request_contact: Optional[bool] = None,

153:        self.request_location: Optional[bool] = request_location
154:        self.request_poll: Optional[KeyboardButtonPollType] = request_poll
155:        self.web_app: Optional[WebAppInfo] = web_app
156:        self.request_users: Optional[KeyboardButtonRequestUsers] = request_users
157:        self.request_chat: Optional[KeyboardButtonRequestChat] = request_chat
158:
159:        self._id_attrs = (
160:            self.text,
161:            self.request_contact,
162:            self.request_location,
163:            self.request_poll,
164:            self.web_app,
165:            self.request_users,
166:            self.request_chat,
167:        )
168:
169:        self._freeze()
170:
171:    @classmethod
172:    def de_json(cls, data: JSONDict, bot: Optional["Bot"] = None) -> "KeyboardButton":
173:        """See :meth:`telegram.TelegramObject.de_json`."""
174:        data = cls._parse_data(data)

176:        data["request_poll"] = de_json_optional(
177:            data.get("request_poll"), KeyboardButtonPollType, bot

179:        data["request_users"] = de_json_optional(
180:            data.get("request_users"), KeyboardButtonRequestUsers, bot
181:        )

183:            data.get("request_chat"), KeyboardButtonRequestChat, bot

185:        data["web_app"] = de_json_optional(data.get("web_app"), WebAppInfo, bot)

19:"""This module contains an object that represents a Telegram ReplyKeyboardMarkup."""
20:
21:from collections.abc import Sequence
22:from typing import Final, Optional, Union
23:
24:from telegram import constants
25:from telegram._keyboardbutton import KeyboardButton
26:from telegram._telegramobject import TelegramObject
27:from telegram._utils.markup import check_keyboard_type
28:from telegram._utils.types import JSONDict
29:
30:
31:class ReplyKeyboardMarkup(TelegramObject):
32:    """This object represents a custom keyboard with reply options. Not supported in channels and
33:    for messages sent on behalf of a Telegram Business account.
34:
35:    Objects of this class are comparable in terms of equality. Two objects of this class are
36:    considered equal, if their size of :attr:`keyboard` and all the buttons are equal.
37:
38:    .. figure:: https://core.telegram.org/file/464001950/1191a/2RwpmgU-swU.123554/b5\
39:        0478c124d5914c23
40:        :align: center
41:
42:        A reply keyboard with reply options.
43:
44:    .. seealso::
45:        Another kind of keyboard would be the :class:`telegram.InlineKeyboardMarkup`.
46:
47:    Examples:
48:        * Example usage: A user requests to change the bot's language, bot replies to the request
49:          with a keyboard to select the new language. Other users in the group don't see
50:          the keyboard.
51:        * :any:`Conversation Bot <examples.conversationbot>`
52:        * :any:`Conversation Bot 2 <examples.conversationbot2>`
53:
54:    Args:
55:        keyboard (Sequence[Sequence[:obj:`str` | :class:`telegram.KeyboardButton`]]): Array of
56:            button rows, each represented by an Array of :class:`telegram.KeyboardButton` objects.
57:        resize_keyboard (:obj:`bool`, optional): Requests clients to resize the keyboard vertically
58:            for optimal fit (e.g., make the keyboard smaller if there are just two rows of
59:            buttons). Defaults to :obj:`False`, in which case the custom keyboard is always of the
60:            same height as the app's standard keyboard.
61:        one_time_keyboard (:obj:`bool`, optional): Requests clients to hide the keyboard as soon as
62:            it's been used. The keyboard will still be available, but clients will automatically
63:            display the usual letter-keyboard in the chat - the user can press a special button in
64:            the input field to see the custom keyboard again. Defaults to :obj:`False`.
65:        selective (:obj:`bool`, optional): Use this parameter if you want to show the keyboard to
66:            specific users only. Targets:
67:
68:            1) Users that are @mentioned in the :attr:`~telegram.Message.text` of the
69:               :class:`telegram.Message` object.
70:            2) If the bot's message is a reply to a message in the same chat and forum topic,
71:                sender of the original message.
72:
73:            Defaults to :obj:`False`.
74:
75:        input_field_placeholder (:obj:`str`, optional): The placeholder to be shown in the input
76:            field when the keyboard is active;
77:            :tg-const:`telegram.ReplyKeyboardMarkup.MIN_INPUT_FIELD_PLACEHOLDER`-
78:            :tg-const:`telegram.ReplyKeyboardMarkup.MAX_INPUT_FIELD_PLACEHOLDER`
79:            characters.
80:
81:            .. versionadded:: 13.7
82:        is_persistent (:obj:`bool`, optional): Requests clients to always show the keyboard when
83:            the regular keyboard is hidden. Defaults to :obj:`False`, in which case the custom
84:            keyboard can be hidden and opened with a keyboard icon.
85:
86:            .. versionadded:: 20.0
87:
88:    Attributes:
89:        keyboard (tuple[tuple[:class:`telegram.KeyboardButton`]]): Array of button rows,
90:            each represented by an Array of :class:`telegram.KeyboardButton` objects.
91:        resize_keyboard (:obj:`bool`): Optional. Requests clients to resize the keyboard vertically
92:            for optimal fit (e.g., make the keyboard smaller if there are just two rows of
93:            buttons). Defaults to :obj:`False`, in which case the custom keyboard is always of the
94:            same height as the app's standard keyboard.
95:        one_time_keyboard (:obj:`bool`): Optional. Requests clients to hide the keyboard as soon as
96:            it's been used. The keyboard will still be available, but clients will automatically
97:            display the usual letter-keyboard in the chat - the user can press a special button in
98:            the input field to see the custom keyboard again. Defaults to :obj:`False`.
99:        selective (:obj:`bool`): Optional. Show the keyboard to specific users only.
100:            Targets:
101:
102:            1) Users that are @mentioned in the :attr:`~telegram.Message.text` of the
103:               :class:`telegram.Message` object.
104:            2) If the bot's message is a reply to a message in the same chat and forum topic,
105:                sender of the original message.
106:
107:            Defaults to :obj:`False`.
108:
109:        input_field_placeholder (:obj:`str`): Optional. The placeholder to be shown in the input
110:            field when the keyboard is active;
111:            :tg-const:`telegram.ReplyKeyboardMarkup.MIN_INPUT_FIELD_PLACEHOLDER`-
112:            :tg-const:`telegram.ReplyKeyboardMarkup.MAX_INPUT_FIELD_PLACEHOLDER`
113:            characters.
114:
115:            .. versionadded:: 13.7
116:        is_persistent (:obj:`bool`): Optional. Requests clients to always show the keyboard when
117:            the regular keyboard is hidden. If :obj:`False`, the custom keyboard can be hidden and
118:            opened with a keyboard icon.
119:
120:            .. versionadded:: 20.0
121:
122:    """
123:
124:    __slots__ = (
125:        "input_field_placeholder",
126:        "is_persistent",
127:        "keyboard",
128:        "one_time_keyboard",
129:        "resize_keyboard",
130:        "selective",
131:    )
132:
133:    def __init__(
134:        self,
135:        keyboard: Sequence[Sequence[Union[str, KeyboardButton]]],
136:        resize_keyboard: Optional[bool] = None,
137:        one_time_keyboard: Optional[bool] = None,
138:        selective: Optional[bool] = None,
139:        input_field_placeholder: Optional[str] = None,
140:        is_persistent: Optional[bool] = None,
141:        *,
142:        api_kwargs: Optional[JSONDict] = None,
143:    ):
144:        super().__init__(api_kwargs=api_kwargs)
145:        if not check_keyboard_type(keyboard):
146:            raise ValueError(
147:                "The parameter `keyboard` should be a sequence of sequences of "
148:                "strings or KeyboardButtons"
149:            )
150:
151:        # Required
152:        self.keyboard: tuple[tuple[KeyboardButton, ...], ...] = tuple(
153:            tuple(KeyboardButton(button) if isinstance(button, str) else button for button in row)
154:            for row in keyboard
155:        )
156:
157:        # Optionals
158:        self.resize_keyboard: Optional[bool] = resize_keyboard
159:        self.one_time_keyboard: Optional[bool] = one_time_keyboard
160:        self.selective: Optional[bool] = selective
161:        self.input_field_placeholder: Optional[str] = input_field_placeholder
162:        self.is_persistent: Optional[bool] = is_persistent
163:
164:        self._id_attrs = (self.keyboard,)
165:
166:        self._freeze()
167:
168:    @classmethod
169:    def from_button(
170:        cls,
171:        button: Union[KeyboardButton, str],
172:        resize_keyboard: bool = False,
173:        one_time_keyboard: bool = False,
174:        selective: bool = False,
175:        input_field_placeholder: Optional[str] = None,
176:        is_persistent: Optional[bool] = None,
177:        **kwargs: object,
178:    ) -> "ReplyKeyboardMarkup":
179:        """Shortcut for::
180:
181:            ReplyKeyboardMarkup([[button]], **kwargs)
182:
183:        Return a ReplyKeyboardMarkup from a single KeyboardButton.
184:
185:        Args:
186:            button (:class:`telegram.KeyboardButton` | :obj:`str`): The button to use in
187:                the markup.
188:            resize_keyboard (:obj:`bool`, optional): Requests clients to resize the keyboard
189:                vertically for optimal fit (e.g., make the keyboard smaller if there are just two
190:                rows of buttons). Defaults to :obj:`False`, in which case the custom keyboard is
191:                always of the same height as the app's standard keyboard.
192:            one_time_keyboard (:obj:`bool`, optional): Requests clients to hide the keyboard as
193:                soon as it's been used. The keyboard will still be available, but clients will
194:                automatically display the usual letter-keyboard in the chat - the user can press
195:                a special button in the input field to see the custom keyboard again.
196:                Defaults to :obj:`False`.
197:            selective (:obj:`bool`, optional): Use this parameter if you want to show the keyboard
198:                to specific users only. Targets:
199:
200:                1) Users that are @mentioned in the text of the Message object.
201:                2) If the bot's message is a reply to a message in the same chat and forum topic,
202:                    sender of the original message.
203:
204:                Defaults to :obj:`False`.
205:
206:            input_field_placeholder (:obj:`str`): Optional. The placeholder shown in the input
207:                field when the reply is active.
208:
209:                .. versionadded:: 13.7
210:            is_persistent (:obj:`bool`): Optional. Requests clients to always show the keyboard
211:                when the regular keyboard is hidden. Defaults to :obj:`False`, in which case the
212:                custom keyboard can be hidden and opened with a keyboard icon.
213:
214:                .. versionadded:: 20.0
215:        """
216:        return cls(
